t:
(a) 
Definition of Net Lease—

        (1) Section 57(c) (relating to definition of net lease) is amended to read as follows:


“(c) 
Net Leases—

“(1) 
In general—For purposes of this section, property shall be considered to be subject to a net lease for a taxable year if—

“(A) 
for such taxable year the sum of the deductions of the lessor with respect to such property which are allowable solely by reason of section 162 (other than rents and reimbursed amounts with respect to such property) is less than 15 percent of the rental income produced by such property, or


“(B) 
the lessor is either guaranteed a specified return or is guaranteed in whole or in part against loss of income.



“(2) 
Multiple leases of single parcel of real property—If a parcel of real property of the taxpayer is leased under two or more leases, paragraph (1) (A) shall, at the election of the tax-payer, be applied by treating all leased portions of such property as subject to a single lease.



“(3) 
Elimination of 15-percent test after 5 years in case of real property—At the election of the taxpayer, paragraph (1) (A) shall not apply with respect to real property of the tax-payer which has been in use for more than 5 years.


“(4) 
Elections—An election under paragraph (2) or (3) shall be made at such time and in such manner as the Secretary or his delegate prescribes by regulations.”




 
        (2) 
Section 163(d) (relating to limitation on interest on investment indebtedness) is amended—

            (A) 
by striking out clause (i) of paragraph (4) (A) and inserting in lieu thereof the following:


“(i) 
for such taxable year the sum of the deductions of the lessor with respect to such property which are allowable solely by reason of section 162 (other than rents and reimbursed amounts with respect to such property) is less than 15 percent of the rental income produced by such property, or”, and



 
            (B) 
by adding at the end thereof the following new paragraph:


“(7) 
Real property leases—For purposes of paragraph (4) (A)—

“(A) 
if a parcel of real property of the taxpayer is leased under two or more leases, paragraph (4) (A) (i) shall, at the election of the taxpayer, be applied by treating all leased portions of such property as subject to a single lease; and


“(B) 
at the election of the taxpayer, paragraph (4)(A)(i) shall not apply with respect to real property of the taxpayer which has been in use for more than 5 years.

An election under subparagraph (A) or (B) shall be made at such time and in such manner as the Secretary or his delegate prescribes by regulations.”



   
    (b) 
Definition of Excess Investment Interest —

        (1) 
Section 57(b)(1) (relating to definition of excess investment interest) is amended by striking out “exceeds the net investment income for the taxable year” and inserting in lieu thereof “exceeds the sum of—

            “(A) 
the net investment income for the taxable year, and
 
            “(B) 
the amount (if any) by which the deductions allowable under sections 162,163,164(a) (1) or 2, and 212 attributable to property of the taxpayer subject to a net lease exceeds the gross rental income produced by such property for the taxable year”.
  
        (2) 
Section 163(d)(1)(B) (relating to limitation on interest on investment indebtedness) is amended to read as follows:


“(B) 
the amount of the net investment income (as defined in paragraph (31(A)), plus the amount (if any) by which the deductions allowable under this section (determined with-out regard to this subsection) and sections 162,164(a) (1) or (2), or 212 attributable to property of the taxpayer subject to a net lease exceeds the rental income produced by such property for the taxable year, plus”.



  
    (c) 
Election by Members of Partnership—Section 703(b) (relating to elections of a partnership) is amended by—

        (1) 
striking out “or” after “(relating to pre–1970 exploration expenditures)” and inserting in lieu thereof a comma; and
 
        (2) 
inserting after “(relating to deduction and recapture of certain mining exploration expenditures)” the following: “under section 57(c) (relating to definition of net lease), or under section 163(d) (relating to limitation on interest on investment indebtedness)”,
  
    (d) Electing Small Business Corporations—Section 57 (b) (2) (C) (relating to items of tax preference) and section 163(d) (3) (C) . (relating to interest on investment indebtedness) are each amended by striking out “sections 164(a)(1) or (2)” and inserting in lieu thereof “sections 162,164(a) (1) or (2)”.
 
    (e) 
Effective Dates—The amendments made by this section to section 57 of the Internal Revenue Code of 1954 shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 1969. The amendments made by this section to section 163 of such Code shall apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 1971.

fable.w: The section directs the Secretary or his delegate to prescribe by regulations the time and manner of taxpayer elections, and under the definition a grant or requirement of rulemaking counts as participation. The tempting reading is that this is only a technical tax amendment defining net leases, with taxpayer elections that resemble applications rather than participation. That reading fails because the regulation-prescribing authority is itself the qualifying feature, regardless of the tax subject matter.
fable.s: shall be made at such time and in such manner as the Secretary or his delegate prescribes by regulations

qwen_block.w: This section defines tax terms and procedures for making elections under the Internal Revenue Code. It does not require the federal government to consult with outside parties, hold public hearings, or form advisory committees with non-federal members. The 'elections' mentioned are unilateral choices by taxpayers to apply certain tax rules, which falls under the exclusion for applications or administrative filings rather than participatory decision-making.
qwen_block.s: An election under paragraph (2) or (3) shall be made at such time and in such manner as the Secretary or his delegate prescribes by regulations.
qwen_block.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the text mentions "elections" made by taxpayers, this constitutes participation. However, the definition explicitly excludes "applications for benefits or grants" and similar administrative filings. An election under tax code provisions is a unilateral choice by a taxpayer to apply a specific rule to their own situation, not a consultation with the government or a public comment period. The government does not "consult" with the taxpayer; the taxpayer simply follows prescribed procedures to make an election. Therefore, this is not participation.

opus.w: The section requires the Secretary of the Treasury to set the timing and manner of taxpayer elections by regulation. Under the definition and Example 6, rulemaking counts as participation because it brings in the public notice-and-comment process. It's tempting to say "No" because this is a technical tax amendment and the 'elections' are just taxpayer choices. But the rulemaking directive alone is enough for "Yes."
opus.s: An election under paragraph (2) or (3) shall be made at such time and in such manner as the Secretary or his delegate prescribes by regulations.
opus.b: 1. **Thinking it through.** At first glance this looks like a "No": it's a technical tax amendment about net leases and investment interest, and no outside party is consulted. The "elections" here are taxpayer choices, not votes or outside input into a federal decision. But the definition counts "requiring rulemaking" as participation, and Example 6 treats any grant of regulatory authority as a "Yes". This section twice directs that elections be made "in such manner as the Secretary or his delegate prescribes by regulations." So the label is "Yes."

qwen_chat.w: This section describes how taxpayers can make elections for tax purposes. The requirement that the Secretary prescribe regulations for these elections is an administrative directive, not a requirement for public participation in the decision-making process. The taxpayer's election is a unilateral action, similar to filing a tax return, and does not involve consultation or coordination with the government before a federal decision is made. The government is not consulting with the public; it is defining the procedure for a private party's administrative choice.
qwen_chat.s: An election under paragraph (2) or (3) shall be made at such time and in such manner as the Secretary or his delegate prescribes by regulations.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that because the Secretary of the Treasury (or his delegate) prescribes regulations for how elections are made, this constitutes rulemaking which often involves public participation. However, the definition explicitly states that "requiring rulemaking" is a form of participation, but merely granting the authority to issue regulations without a specific mandate for public comment or consultation in this specific section is not enough. More importantly, the core activity here is a taxpayer making an election for their own tax liability. This is an administrative procedure for applying tax law to a specific taxpayer, akin to filing a return or an application. It does not involve the government consulting with outsiders before making a general policy decision. The "election" is a unilateral choice by the taxpayer, not a collaborative process with the government. The government's role is to define the rules, not to participate in the decision with the taxpayer.
